newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails three Tibetans for separatism.
newsitem.headline: China jails three Tibetans for separatism.

text.p: A Chinese court has sentenced three Tibetans, including two former officials, to jail terms of up to six years for separatist activities and leaking state secrets, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Qazha Qamba Chilai, 58, former vice-chairman of the Tibet Autonomous Regional Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, received the heaviest sentence, Xinhua said. The conference is an advisory group to parliament.
A second official Qamba Qung and Samzhub, a businessman, were sentenced to four and two years in prison respectively, Xinhua said.
The sentences were handed down on April 21, it said without giving a reason for the delay in reporting them.

The defendants "colluded with separatist forces abroad. They have seriously jeopardised the national unification and unity of ethnic groups, damaged the stability and development of Tibet and have committed the crime of splitting the country", the verdict said.
The court "diminished the penalties of the three accused on the charge of conspiring to split the country", Xinhua said. It did not elaborate.
